title: RET Module 1: Actuarial work and retirement benefits applications
name: Actuarial work and retirement benefits applications
intro: The primary audience for the FCIA modules is individuals who desire to be admitted as Fellows of the CIA.
Individuals seeking continuing professional development credit can also register for the FCIA modules.

Each FCIA candidate through Pathways 1 and 2 is required to complete both FCIA modules, while Pathway 3 candidates will have to complete the second module. It is anticipated that FCIA module candidates will have six months from the date of module purchase to complete each FCIA module. As a general guideline, candidates should allocate approximately 100 hours to complete all activities included in a module.

outcomes.text: Describe risk including insurable risk.
Provide examples of types of insurable risks and classes of life insurance that respond to insurable risk.
Describe and provide examples of perils and hazards.
Explain the conflicts that can arise in the objectives of risk management.
Identify and describe the five steps of the risk management process:
bullets: a. Step 1 – Identifying and analyzing exposures.
c. Step 3 – Selecting the best technique.
d. Step 4 – Implementing the risk management plan.
e. Step 5 – Monitoring results and modifying the plan.

outcomes.text: Describe the basic insurance relationship of pooling funds to pay losses.
Explain the major functions of insurance:
Identify and describe categories of insurance.
Identify and describe categories of retirement schemes.
Describe the different forms of insurance companies (e.g., stock companies, mutuals, government insurers, captive insurance companies).
Explain financial stability and returns for insurers, including the differences for stock companies and mutuals.
Describe the major functions of an insurance company, including:
Describe basic insurance administration and how actuaries are involved.
Describe underwriting regimes, applications for insurance, preferred criteria, and screening tests, and how they relate to selection of risk.
For reinsurance:
bullets: a. Explain the purpose of reinsurance.
b. Describe the primary methods and types of reinsurance.
c. Describe the main reinsurance contract provisions.

outcomes.text: Describe the roles and responsibilities of actuaries in insurance companies.
Describe the traditional functions of a consulting firm:
bullets: a. Administration and consulting of pension plans.
c. Actuarial valuation and financial reporting requirements.
d. Benefit plan design and amendments.
f. Appointed Actuary tasks and responsibilities.
i. Sales and distribution of insurance.

outcomes.text: Describe the roles and responsibilities of actuaries in consulting firms.
Describe basic insurance products:
Describe key issues related to customers of insurance products.
Describe the traditional functions of an actuary operating in corporations, including role and responsibilities within these functions:
Understand the importance of global compensation for a corporation, including its impact on hiring, retention, attrition, succession planning, etc.
Understand the different departments within a company that interact with global compensation actuaries, such as:
bullets: d. Human resources (HR), including labor relations (LR).

outcomes.text: Outline the roles and responsibilities of actuaries in company departments identified in 3. within the global compensation strategy, such as:
bullets: a. Actuarial valuations for accounting purposes.
d. Plan text drafting and amendments.

topics.title: The Canadian retirement environment and professionalism

outcomes.text: Describe and understand the three pillars of the Canadian retirement system and their utilization to optimize personal wealth and retirement income.
bullets: a. Public plans such as the Canada Pension Plan and Québec Pension Plan.
i. Registered vehicles such as RRSP and TFSA.

outcomes.text: Explain how employer-provided plans coordinate with public plans in Canada.
Analyze the challenges facing public plans in Canada.
bullets: a. Evaluate alternative proposals for facing those challenges.

outcomes.text: Determine the aggregate benefit to the employee from an employer-provided and public plan.
Describe how public retirement benefits, personal savings, and employer pension plans can be used to maximize benefits and manage longevity risks.
Understand the Canadian retirement legislative framework.
Understand the role and responsibilities of the actuary in the Canadian retirement system.
Describe and explain how guarantee funds such as Assuris and Ontario’s Pensions Benefits Guarantee Fund (PBGF) operate.
Understand the application of the CIA Standards of Practice and Rules of Professional Conduct.

topics.title: The U.S. retirement environment and professionalism

outcomes.text: Understand the retirement system in the United States.
Understand the U.S. retirement legislative framework.
Explain how employer-provided plans coordinate with social insurance plans in the United States.
Determine the aggregate benefit to the employee from an employer-provided and social insurance plan.
Explain and apply guidelines to Professional Conduct.
Explain and apply relevant qualifications standards.
Explain and apply the applicable standards of practice related to valuing retirement obligations.
Compare the Canadian and U.S. retirement systems.
Describe the role of actuaries in family law, including the valuation of pension plan benefits in marriage (relationship) breakdown.

Describe the role of actuaries in civil litigation, including damages in personal injuries, fatalities, wrongful termination, insurance and reinsurance disputes, pension disputes, and other litigation.
Describe the role conferred to actuaries by the Criminal Code of Canada in calculating the criminal rate of interest.
Describe and distinguish the roles and responsibilities of a fact witness, an expert witness, and a provider of litigation advice.
Describe the context provided by the common law, legislation, and the rules of civil procedure on actuarial evidence practice.

Describe the role of CIA Rules of Professional Conduct and Standards of Practice (Part 1000, general, and Part 4000, actuarial evidence) in guiding the professionalism of actuarial evidence practice. Show awareness of the importance of professionalism for actuaries whose actuarial evidence practice is incidental to full-time practice in another actuarial practice area, such as insurance or pensions.

Describe the functions fulfilled by other professionals in the litigation area, such as life-care planners, vocational experts, accountants, economists, engineers, personal financial planners, business valuators, appraisers, and structured settlement brokers, and how these professionals complement and compete with the function of actuaries in actuarial evidence.
